G2_boundary_bit_exactness.disagreement: None found, but for a structural reason rather than a substantive one: G2's bit-exactness holds for ANY bound value substituted in this way, self-authored or real-external, because AT_*_BOUNDARY test snapshots are constructed as v := lo (or v := hi) and IEEE-754 subtraction of a float from itself is exact for every finite double. G2 passing is therefore a tautological property of the fixture's test-case construction method, not evidence that the module's tolerance MODEL (nominal ratio +/- band) matches any real published source -- that question is answered by G3, not G2. Recording this as a scope-boundary finding: G2 is not capable of detecting the kind of sourcing defect this item is attacking.
G2_boundary_bit_exactness.method: G2 asserts that a KAT test_case tagged AT_LOWER_BOUNDARY/AT_UPPER_BOUNDARY has binding_margin bit-exact 0.0 f64. This is checked here by substituting this fire's real, externally-sourced Hexion bounds (32.0, 36.0 pbw) for the fixture's self-authored bounds and re-deriving the same equality.

The closest, Hexion EPIKOTE L20/EPIKURE 960 (-5.55%/+6.25%), is far closer to symmetric +/-5% than the 4 WEST SYSTEM bands, but still fails both the exact-symmetric and exact-+/-5% checks G3 requires. 0 of 5 real sources match the module's G3 assumption; G3 would REJECT all 5 if substituted for the fixture's self-authored numbers.
G3_tolerance_band_construction.method: The module's own oracle (benchmarks/constraint-envelope-oracle-v1/run_envelope_gates.py, gate G3) asserts every envelope's tolerance band is a symmetric +/-5%-by-mass-per-part window (TOL_FRAC=0.05, checked via is_5pct). This re-score applies that identical G3 arithmetic to all 5 real, named, explicit tolerance bands now located (WEST SYSTEM 105/205, 105/206, 105/207, 105/209 by Gougeon Brothers, plus Hexion EPIKOTE L20/EPIKURE 960) instead of the fixture's self-authored numbers.

G4_ratio_consistency.disagreement: G4, as actually implemented, cannot and does not detect envelope_id/nominal-mass ratio mismatches regardless of whether the nominal values originate from the self-authored fixture or from real external supplier data -- the code path simply does not exist. The disagreement is between the oracle's own docstring claim ('and ratio-string consistency') and its actual behavior, not between sourced and unsourced data.

finding.consequence: This is the root cause of fire 1's internal defect finding (dgeba-pacm-marine-topcoat-100to30: envelope_id says 100:30, recorded nominal masses are 200.0g:30.0g) passing G4 silently: G4 was never capable of catching it, contrary to what the oracle's own docstring claims it does.
finding.finding: The oracle's own module docstring (run_envelope_gates.py) states G4 'checks nominal part_A + part_B == total and ratio-string consistency', but the actual implementation (`g4_pass = all(e["nominal_parts_sum_to_total"] for e in per_env)`) only ever checks the additive-sum property; no code path compares envelope_id's declared ratio string against nominal_part_a_g/nominal_part_b_g anywhere in the file. This is confirmed by direct source read this fire, independent of any external data sourcing.

G4_ratio_consistency.method: Re-examine G4 (benchmarks/constraint-envelope-oracle-v1/run_envelope_gates.py) against this fire's newly confirmed oracle-source finding.

G5_tamper_battery.disagreement: Not re-scorable against externally-sourced tolerance bands: G5's probes mutate STRUCTURE (inverted bounds, missing trust flags, injected claims) rather than substitute alternative nominal/tolerance VALUES, so swapping in Hexion's or WEST SYSTEM's real numbers exercises no different code path than the fixture's self-authored numbers already do. Recording this honestly as N/A-by-design rather than silently omitting G5: the item's re-score requirement is satisfied for G5 by establishing that no sourcing-dependent disagreement is possible here, not by finding one.
G5_tamper_battery.method: G5 runs a 12-probe tamper battery (policy substitution, trusted-feature substitution, bound inversion, inclusive-boundary drift, candidate gate-pass injection, authority-lock preservation) against a fixed base envelope (dgeba-teta-primer-9to1) and its own synthetically-mutated policies/snapshots.

internal_self_consistency_defects.defect: envelope_id declares a 100:30 ratio, but the envelope's own nominal_part_a_g/nominal_part_b_g are 200.0/30.0 (a 200:30, i.e. ~100:15, ratio) -- the id-declared ratio and the recorded nominal masses disagree with each other. internal_self_consistency_defects.oracle_gap: G4 (nominal_parts_sum_to_total in run_envelope_gates.py) checks only that nominal_part_a_g + nominal_part_b_g == nominal_total_g (200+30==230, TRUE); it never checks that the envelope_id's stated ratio matches the recorded nominal masses, so this defect passes every check the module's own oracle runs.

All 4 real, named, explicit tolerance bands located this fire (WEST SYSTEM 105/205, 105/206, 105/207, 105/209) are asymmetric and diverge from +/-5% by up to 4x on one side.

proposed_followups.defect: The oracle's module docstring (benchmarks/constraint-envelope-oracle-v1/run_envelope_gates.py) claims G4 'checks nominal part_A + part_B == total and ratio-string consistency', but the implementation (`g4_pass = all(e["nominal_parts_sum_to_total"] for e in per_env)`) only ever checks the additive-sum property. No code path compares envelope_id's declared ratio string against the recorded nominal masses. This is why the dgeba-pacm-marine-topcoat-100to30 id/data mismatch (found fire 1) is invisible to G4.
proposed_followups.proposed_done_criterion: Either add a real ratio-string-consistency check to G4's implementation (parsing envelope_id's declared ratio and comparing it to nominal_part_a_g/nominal_part_b_g within a stated tolerance) or correct the docstring to stop claiming a check the code does not perform.

verdict_basis: Unchanged from fire 1's finding, now confirmed against a broader, done_criterion-meeting sweep: the claim under attack asserts the fail-closed metrics' population is drawn from published formulations. Across 13 named, queried sources this fire and fire 1 combined: (1) 3 of the fixture's 10 envelopes (30% of the envelope population) cite named supplier products whose real, located technical data sheets state a materially different nominal mix ratio -- deviations larger than the module's own asserted +/-5% QC tolerance; (2) 1 envelope cites a product combination absent from the real located TDS; (3) 1 envelope has an internal id/data ratio defect; (4) the module's G4 gate cannot catch (3) because its docstring overclaims a 'ratio-string consistency' check its implementation never performs (new finding, this fire); (5) the module's G3 gate's foundational symmetric +/-5% assumption disagrees with all 5 real, named, explicit tolerance bands now located (0/5 match); (6) G2's apparent 'boundary bit-exactness' guarantee is a tautology of test-case construction, not evidence the tolerance model matches real data; (7) G5's tamper battery is orthogonal to nominal-value sourcing by design. The population underlying this module's fail-closed metrics is not a reliable re-derivation of published formulations.
